Norovirus Outbreak Disrupts Czech Transportation & Logistics Operations

A widespread norovirus outbreak is currently impacting the Transportation & Logistics industry across the Czech Republic, with significant operational slowdowns reported since the start of the week. Dopravni Podnik Hlm Prahy AS, one of the country’s leading urban transport providers, is among the companies affected, with absenteeism rates among drivers, maintenance staff and depot workers rising sharply.

According to the Czech Association of Transport Operators, over 15% of industry employees in the Prague region have been unable to report for work since Monday, after clusters of gastrointestinal illness were confirmed at several bus and tram depots. The majority of affected workers are experiencing severe symptoms typical of norovirus, including vomiting, diarrhea and dehydration.

“In the last 48 hours, we have seen a sudden spike in sick calls from operational staff, especially in Prague and Brno,” said Jan Kolar, spokesperson for the association. “This is causing major schedule disruptions, with up to 20% of regular services running late or being cancelled altogether in some areas.”

Dopravni Podnik Hlm Prahy AS has implemented emergency cleaning protocols at its depots and vehicles, and has adjusted staff rosters to maintain core services. “Our priority is to protect the health of both passengers and employees,” said Martina Stehlikova, a company spokesperson. “We are working closely with health authorities, and we ask for public understanding as we may need to reduce service frequencies at short notice.”

Smaller logistics firms such as Cestovni Express SRO have also reported delays in deliveries, as warehouse and driving staff have been sent home with symptoms or placed in precautionary isolation. “We are running at about 75% capacity,” said Petr Novak, general manager at Cestovni Express SRO. “We are prioritizing medical and essential goods, but non-urgent shipments are being rescheduled.”

Analysts warn that if the outbreak continues, the disruptions could have a cascading effect on the movement of goods and people within the country, especially as the busy summer travel season approaches. “The Czech transportation network is highly interconnected,” said Klara Vavrova, a transport sector analyst. “Even localized outbreaks can quickly affect regional and national schedules. The full impact will depend on how swiftly companies can contain the illness and restore staffing levels.”

At time of writing, health officials have not set a date for the lifting of additional workplace hygiene measures. Further updates are expected as local authorities monitor the situation.
